questions: Did this walking problem begin suddenly, within the last few days?
Do you have new weakness or numbness on one side of your body?
Have you had facial drooping, trouble speaking, or sudden vision changes?
Have you recently fallen or been unable to walk without assistance?
Do you have severe back pain with weakness or numbness in both legs?
Have you lost control of your bladder or bowels?
Do you feel dizzy or as though the room is spinning when you walk?
Do you have pain in either leg or foot when standing or walking?
Do your legs feel stiff, cramped, or difficult to move?
Do you have shaking or tremors when your hands or legs are at rest?
Have you noticed worsening balance or coordination over weeks or months?
Do you have numbness or reduced sensation in both feet?
Have you recently had an infection, injury, surgery, or hospitalization?
Do you have diabetes, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson’s disease, or a previous stroke?
Are you taking any new medicines that make you sleepy, weak, or unsteady?
results: 1. bedside eye-movement exam: vertical gaze palsy progressing to complete external ophthalmoplegia
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Anti-Ri (ANNA-2)–associated paraneoplastic brainstem encephalitis causing progressive external ophthalmoplegia and gait dysfunction, most likely due to an occult breast or gynecologic carcinoma.

ALTERNATIVE: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP).

ALTERNATIVE: Anti-Ma2–associated paraneoplastic brainstem/diencephalic encephalitis.

ALTERNATIVE: Miller Fisher syndrome or another immune-mediated ophthalmoplegic neuropathy.
dx: Anti-Ri (ANNA-2)–associated paraneoplastic brainstem encephalitis causing progressive external ophthalmoplegia and gait dysfunction, most likely due to an occult breast or gynecologic carcinoma.
